scope: Policy iteration as Newton's method and its convergence rates, for finite state spaces and arbitrary (possibly infinite) policy sets with a greedy selector: the Bellman and policy operators as sup-norm contractions, the Newton identity, monotone improvement; the linear rate ||v* - v_{k+1}|| <= beta ||v* - v_k||, the Puterman-Brumelle bound (1 - beta)||v* - v_{greedy v}|| <= beta delta ||v* - v||, quadratic convergence under Lipschitz greedy transitions, superlinear convergence under continuity, finite termination when greedy policies near v* are optimal; for finite MDPs, the optimality gap, optimality of greedy policies within g/(2 beta + 1) of v*, and termination of policy iteration with an explicit iteration bound.
source: Howard (1960); Puterman and Brumelle (1979); Santos and Rust (2004).
